_what: Test files that do not run on one platform, each with the reason. vitest.config.ts excludes them on that platform only and prints SKIPPED (not a pass) for every one, so a Windows run says what it did not judge. tests/platform-exclusions.test.ts fails on an entry without a reason, on a file that no longer exists, and on any platform other than win32. Every entry here still runs on Linux (quality-gates-fast) and macOS (quality:macos). Shrink this list; never grow it to make a red run green without a reason that is about the platform rather than about the code.

win32.tests/release-suite/observer-cleanup.tes: drives scripts/quality/suite/observers.sh with POSIX ps/kill/nettop; the Windows lane samples sockets in windows.ps1 and never sources observers.sh
win32.tests/release-windows/remote-from-sha.te: tests scripts/release-windows-remote.sh, which runs on the Mac and drives the Windows host over ssh; it is not meant to run on Windows
win32.tests/ui-register.test.ts: #908: scripts/quality/ui-register.mjs resolves imports and handlers with POSIX path joins, so on Windows it follows fewer chains and writes a different register; the register is generated and checked on Linux and macOS
win32.tests/release-suite/ui-walk.test.ts: #908: builds its walk from the generated UI register (walkTargets), which the Windows run reads as empty for the same POSIX path reason; the real S5 walk of the built app is judged by the release suite
